sentences.text: 1. Vide this judgment, this Court shall decide suit filed by the plaintiff for possession and mandatory injunction.

2. Brief facts as per the plaint are as under:-
2.1. The plaintiff is the legal owner of residential plot bearing no. GA-113, Pul Prahaladpur, Badarpur, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as 'suit property').

The defendant is resident of Plot No. GA-114, Pul Prahaladpur, Badarpur, New Delhi,
adjacent to the plot of the plaintiff.

The plot of the defendant is admeasuring 110 sq.
yds. and out of 110 sq. yds, the defendant had already sold 30 sq. yds. to one third person and now the defendant is owner of the plot measuring 80 sq. yds.
2.2.

The plaintiff has purchased the suit property from Sh.
Doji S/o Sh. Naganga, R/o F-70, Vishwakarma Colony, New Delhi, in the year 2001 by virtue of valid sale documents.
All original papers of land/plot and possession of the plot was handed over to the plaintiff by seller Sh. Doji and the plaintiff was in possession of the plot since 30.07.2007.

sentences.text: The plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit property and since the day of purchase, the plaintiff was in exclusive possession of the same.
Thereafter, the plaintiff has covered the suit property by constructing boundary walls and also constructed a small room with two doors on east and west side.
The plaintiff regularly visited the suit property almost every month.

2.4. On 30.07.2007, the plaintiff had came to know that the defendant (Gulab Singh) was illegally acquiring/grabbing plaintiff's entire plot by removing the back door/gate of the room and by constructing new boundary wall.
The plaintiff immediately rushed towards his plot and was shocked to see that the entire plot was illegally grabbed by the defendant, who was also present there.

On asking to vacate and hand over peaceful possession of the plot, the defendant started abusing and threatened the plaintiff with dire consequences in the case plaintiff again visited the suit property.
The defendant said that he had already illegally grabbed the entire suit property and he would not vacate the suit property at any cost.
The defendant extended threat to the life of the plaintiff in case if he approached police or court.
The wife of the defendant also abused the plaintiff.
The defendant illegally acquired and forcefully took the possession of the suit property of the plaintiff and also illegally restrained the plaintiff to enter and use his plot.
Thereafter, the matter was reported to PS Sangam Vihar, New Delhi on 30.07.2007.
On the information of the plaintiff, the officials of PS Sangam Vihar registered an FIR No. 755/2007 dated 30.07.2007 against the defendant.
Thereafter the defendant was arrested in the said FIR.
2.5. The defendant had grabbed the entire plot of plaintiff and despite repeated requests, the defendant failed to hand over the possession of the suit property.

Since 30.07.2007, the defendant has caused a monetary loss of Rs. 3000/- per month to the plaintiff by illegally using and retaining the possession of suit property of which the plaintiff is the legal owner.
The plaintiff has approached various authorities and the police officials requesting them to restore the possession of the suit property.

In the month of April 2011, the plaintiff again approached to the defendant and requested to hand over the possession of suit property but the defendant refused to do so and he threatened to dispose of the suit property.
2.6. The plaintiff has come to know that the defendant is planning to sell his entire property and the entire plot of the plaintiff to the third party.
Since 30.07.2007, the defendant is in illegal/wrongful possession of the suit property.

The defendant has retained the suit property of the plaintiff and caused monetary loss to the plaintiff which the plaintiff is entitled to recover from the defendant including the mesne profit since 30.07.2007 till the recovery of the possession of the suit property.

Hence, the present suit has been filed seeking following relief:-
"a) Pass a decree in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant restoring the possession of the plaintiff in the suit property directing therein the defendant, his agents, family members, attorneys and legal representatives to hand over the vacant,
peaceful possession of the suit property bearing no. G-113, Pul Prahaladpur,
Badarpur, New Delhi, admea- suring 50 sq. yards, part of Khasra No. 388, Tehsil Kalkaji, South District, New Delhi (more specifically shown Red in colour in the attached site plan),

2 b) Pass a decree of mandatory injunction in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant directing therein the de- fendant, his agents, family members, attorneys and legal representatives be restrained from interference in the legal possession of the plaintiff with regard to the suit property."
3. Summons were issued to the defendant.

4. The defendant contested the present suit on the following grounds:-
4.1. The present suit filed by the plaintiff is frivolous suit and there is no cause of action arising in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant qua the subject-matter of the suit as the defendant is only in possession of his property and the defendant has not encroached/trespassed upon the property of the plaintiff.
The defendant is not in possession of any part of the plaintiff's property.
4.2. The present suit filed by the plaintiff is grossly undervalued as the market value of the suit property is much more.

The defendant is the lawful owner of property admeasuring 110 sq. yards bearing no. GA-114, Pul Prahladpur, Badarpur, Delhi and has been in continuous peaceful possession of the same for last more than 30 years.
The plaintiff has already implicated the defendant and his wife in a false criminal case which is pending adjudication in the Saket Courts.

The plaintiff has alleged that he was dispossessed way back in the month of July 2007 and it is clearly a case of active acquiescence on the part of the plaintiff as he did not file any civil suit for 4 years.
The plaintiff is trying to harass the defendant who is a poor man sustaining himself and his family by working as daily wage labourer.
4.3. The defendant has denied that he had sold 30 sq. yards out of 110 sq. yards.
The defendant is still in peaceful and exclusive possession of 110 sq. yards of property.
The defendant did nothing on that particular day and the plaintiff has made a false and bogus complaint with the local police.

The plaintiff and one of his friends wanted to grab the property of the defendant and to achieve that end,
they have implicated the defendant in this suit and also in a criminal case.
4.4. It is unfortunate that at the instance of the plaintiff and one other person who is the land mafia of the locality, the defendant got arrested in false criminal case.
The defendant has nothing to do with the plaintiff's property.

The defendant is neither the owner of the suit property nor he is in possession of any party of the plaintiff's property and therefore, there is no question of interfering with the possession/ownership of the plaintiff's property in any manner.
There is no question of the defendant being ejected out of plaintiff's property as the defendant is in possession of only his property and not the plaintiff's property.
5. No replication was filed by the plaintiff.

9. Arguments on behalf of the Plaintiff.
9.1.

Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff would argue that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit property and he had purchased the suit property from Sh. Doji by virtue of registered documents in the year 2001 and the defendant is resident of adjoining property no. GA-114 measuring 80 sq. yards.
The defendant was earlier in possession of land measuring 110 sq. yards however, 30 sq. yards land was sold by him.

On 30.07.2007, the defendant had removed back door of the room and the boundary wall of the suit property and the defendant had merged property of the plaintiff with his property and he has dispossessed the plaintiff.
In his WS, the defendant has admitted that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit property.

During cross-examination of the plaintiff, suggestion was given to him that the suit has been filed by him 4 years after dispossession when he realized that the criminal case was going to be decided against him.

This suggestion given by Ld. counsel for defendant is an Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/

sentences.text: Another suggestion has been given to the plaintiff, "It is wrong to suggest that presently Mr. Jitender Nath Sinha is in possession of the suit property".
However it was never the case of the defendant that some third party was in possession of the suit property.
The said suggestion given by the defendant would make it clear that after grabbing the suit property, the defendant had placed one Jitender Nath Sinha in the suit property.
The defendant in his evidence has not challenged the existence of the suit property or dimensions or locations or even prior possession of the plaintiff.

Another suggestion has been given to PW1 by the defendant, "It is further wrong to suggest that in any case, if the defendant was in possession of any property apart from his property bearing no.
GA-114, the same is not the plaintiff's property".

Throughout the trial, the defendant has not taken defence that he was in possession of some other property apart from his property bearing no.
GA-114, and this suggestion amounts to admission on the part of the defendant that he is in occupation of another property apart from his own property.
Counsel for the plaintiff would further argue that the plaintiff has also examined previous owner Sh. Doji as PW-2.
No suggestion has been given to PW-2 that he had not sold the suit property of the plaintiff or that he had not placed the plaintiff in possession thereof.
The plaintiff has also examined Sh. Jai Prakash from the office of SDM who has prepared the report Ex.PW4/1. PW-4

has proved the photographs that the defendant had broken the intervening wall between his property and plaintiff's property and merged the property of the plaintiff with his (defendant's)
property.
The photographs filed by PW-4 were not disputed by Ld. counsel for the defendant during the cross- examination of PW-4.
The plaintiff has been able to prove that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit property which is duly identified.
The plaintiff is no longer in possession of the suit property.

In evidence, the defendant has tried to set up a different defence that the plaintiff has sold the suit property to one Sh. Jitender Nath Sinha and that Jitender Nath Sinha is in possession of the suit property whereas he has not been able to prove his defence.
It is a defendant who is in actual possession of the suit property of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has been able to prove his case on preponderance of probability.
Hence, the suit of the plaintiff may be decreed.
10. Arguments on behalf of the Defendant.
Counsel for the defendant would argue that the plaintiff is a rich and influential person whereas the defendant is a poor man.
PW-2 Doji in conspiracy with one person had trespassed in the defendant's property and attempted to rape the defendant's wife regarding which FIR u/s 376 IPC was registered against Doji.

In order to take revenge, Doji has entered in criminal conspiracy with Asgar Ali and got registered false FIR against defendant Gulab Singh and his wife on 28.02.2001 and in that FIR, it was claimed that Asgar Ali was tenant in house no. GA 113 Pul Prahladpur (suit property) and on 28.02.2001, the defendant alongwith his wife broke adjoining wall which separated their houses and tenant was thrown out of the house with his household articles.
The defendant and his wife were acquitted in the said case.
The plaintiff has claimed that he had built a boundary wall and room in the suit property after purchasing it.

However, PW-2 Doji has contradicted it by deposing that he had built the boundary wall and one room in the suit property Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/

It is further argued that the suit property never belonged to the plaintiff and presently, it is a multi story building of 5 floors which has been purchased by several persons for valuable consideration.

After coming to the know about this fact, the defendant has filed an appropriate application to bring the relevant documents on record but the said application was dismissed by this Court and the defendant, being a poor person, could not afford to challenge the said order before Hon'ble High Court.

The plaintiff has not been able to prove his ownership of the suit property as the Will has not been proved by calling any of the attesting witness and the GPA does not confer any title and the GPA is also without any consideration.

11. Issue-wise Findings of the Court 12.

Issue No. 1 : Whether the defendant has grabbed the property of plaintiff bearing Plot no.
GA-113, Pul Prahaladpur, Badarpur, New Delhi, on or before 30.07.07?
The onus to prove this issue was on the plaintiff.

The plaintiff has claimed that he has purchased the suit property from Sh. Doji in the year 2001 vide registered GPA and Will dated 07.07.2001 and the physical possession of the plot was handed over to him.
Thereafter, he had constructed a small room and boundary wall in the property.

On 30.07.2007, he came to know that the defendant was illegally acquiring /
grabbing his entire plot by removing the back door / gate of the room and by raising new boundary wall.
When he reached to the suit property, he was shocked to see that the plot was illegally grabbed by the defendant.
The defendant threatened him and said that he had grabbed the entire property and he would not vacate the suit property at any cost.

12.2. The defendant has taken defence that he is only in possession of his property and he has not encroached/trespassed upon the property of the plaintiff and that he is not in possession of any part of the plaintiff's property.

12.3. The burden is upon the plaintiff to prove that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit property and that the defendant had encroached upon/ grabbed the property of the plaintiff ad- measuring 50 Sq.
yards.

In order to prove his case, the plaintiff has examined himself as PW-1, previous owner Sh.
Doji as PW-2 and Kanoongo Sh. Jai Prakash as PW-4.
12.4.

The plaintiff has relied upon the registered GPA dated 07.07.2001 executed by Sh. Doji in his favour as Ex. PW1/1, registered Will executed by Doji in his favour as Ex. PW1/2, site plan as Ex.
PW1/3, photographs of the suit property showing illegal grabbing by the defendant as Ex. PW1/4,
the FIR registered by him regarding trespass as Ex. PW1/5 and report of Kanungo PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash as Ex. PW1/6.
The plaintiff has filed documents i.e. registered GPA and Will executed by Sh. Doji in his favour in respect of the suit property.
The plaintiff has examined Sh. Doji as PW2.

However, no title Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/
6 document of the suit property in favour of Sh. Doji has been proved on record.

sentences.text: Mere execution of GPA and Will by Sh. Doji in favour of plaintiff Sh. Babu Lal in respect of the suit property is not sufficient to prove that Sh. Doji had right, title or interest in the suit property or that he had any authority to transfer or sell the suit property to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has claimed himself to be the owner of the suit property on the basis of GPA and Will.
These documents do not confer title.
The plaintiff has failed to prove that he had title over the suit property or that he is the owner of the suit property.
12.6. The plaintiff has to discharge the onus that the defendant had broken the boundary wall of the suit property ad- measuring 50 Sq Yards and grabbed his property.
12.7. PW1 has relied upon the report of Kanoongo to prove that the defendant had grabbed the suit property.
The report of Kanoongo is Ex. PW1/6.
The plaintiff has examined Sh. Jai Prakash who had prepared report Ex. PW1/6 as PW4.

PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash has stated that he has demarcated the property in question i.e. GA-113 and GA-114, Khasra No. 388, Village Pul Prahladpur, New Delhi on 05.12.2012 as per the directions of the Court and prepared report which is Ex. PW4/1 and he had denoted the disputed property in green colour in the site plan which is part of his report.
12.8.
In his cross examination, PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash has stated that the disputed property which he has shown in green colour in the site plan is the house no. GA 113 and GA 114.
House no. GA 113 ad-measures about 50 square yards.
The defendant is in possession of 120 square yards whereas on papers he is the owner of only 110 square yards.
The defendant Gulab Singh has encroached upon the entire property of the plaintiff i.e. all 50 square yards.
The plaintiff is not in possession of his property.

12.9. PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash was asked by Ld. Counsel for the defendant to see his report and thereafter show whether he had mentioned anywhere in his report that the defendant has in any manner encroached upon the property of the plaintiff.

After seeing his report Ex. PW4/1, PW4 Sh.
Jai Prakash has answered that he has nowhere mentioned in his report that the defendant has encroached upon any piece of land belonging to the plaintiff.

Perusal of file would show that vide order dated 04.08.2011, SDM was directed to conduct demarcation of the suit property bearing plot no. GA-113, part of Khasra no. 388, Pul Prahladpur,
Badarpur, New Delhi.
Thereafter, report alongwith the documents were filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash, Kanungo on 08.05.2012.
The Court had only directed Tehsildar to demarcate the suit property no. GA-113.
However, report Ex. PW4/1 given by Tehsildar is also about encroachment in the property of the plaintiff by the defendant.

No such direction was given to the Tehsildar /
Kanungo to decide as to whether the defendant had encroached on the property of the plaintiff.

The report of Tehsildar, "mauka dekhne se aisa praateet hota hai ki disputed plot ki chaar diwari tod kar Sh. Gulab Singh ne apne plot ke sath aapas mein mila rakha hai" is not in consonance with the direction given to SDM by this Court.
The said portion of the report has been mentioned without directions by the Court to the SDM to ascertain upon the encroachment and the said portion of the report cannot be believed.

Further, as already mentioned above, during cross examination, PW4 Sh.
Jai Prakash has admitted that he has nowhere mentioned in his report that the the defendant had Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/
7 encroached upon any piece of land belonging to the plaintiff.

sentences.text: The testimony of PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash would prove that as per documents of the defendant, he is the owner of land measuring 110 sq. yards, however, when measurement was done for demarcation, it was found that Gulab Singh was in possession of the land measuring 120 square yards.
The case of the plaintiff is that the defendant has encroached upon the suit property which is ad-measuring 50 Sq Yards.
However the report of PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash and his testimony would prove that the defendant is in possession of extra 10 Sq Yards only apart from his own property which is measuring 110 sq. yards.
The measurement of the disputed portion shown in green colour in the site plan of the report Ex. PW4/1 is not mentioned by PW4.

The report Ex. PW1/6 (also Ex.
PW4/1) and testimony of PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash
do not prove that this extra 10 Sq yards of land in possession of the defendant is the suit property of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has also relied upon the photographs which are filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash alongwith the report.

The photographs filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash alongwith his report are Ex.
DW1/PX1 and Ex. DW1/PX2.
In the photograph Ex. DW1/PX2, one person is standing in front of one property and on his back, one door is visible.
During cross examination of the defendant, the photographs filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash were shown to him.

After seeing the photograph Ex.
DW1/PX1, DW1 Gulab Singh has stated that property at point X in photograph Ex. DW1/PX1 is his property and when he was shown portion Y (with door and window) in the photograph Ex.DW-1/PX1, he has denied that point Y was the suit property or that the same was in possession of the plaintiff.
DW1 has further stated that GA-113 is adjacent to the property as shown at point Y.

The photographs filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash alongwith report by itself is not sufficient to establish that the defendant had grabbed the property of the plaintiff measuring 50 Sq Yards or that point Y is the property of the plaintiff.

Further, if the photographs of the suit property Ex.PW1/4 (colly) filed by the plaintiff are compared with the photographs filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash, it would show that the property of the plaintiff is entirely different from its front from the front of the point Y in the photograph Ex.DW-1/PX1.
12.15.

On 29.01.2026, clarification was taken from the plaintiff regarding the photographs Ex.PW-1/4 and the plaintiff stated that the photograph no. 1 was showing front of the suit property and photograph no. 2 was back of the suit property and that now back side of the suit property has been whitewashed by the defendant.

From the photographs on record, it can not be ascertained that the photographs filed by the plaintiff and the property at point Y of photograph Ex. DW1/PX1 filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash are of one and the same property.
12.17.
As per the case of the plaintiff, the defendant had grabbed the suit property by allegedly removing the boundary wall on the back side and by removing the back door of the room.

It is not the case of the plaintiff that windows and doors in the front of the suit property were also removed and they were reinstalled at different place by the defendant so as to completely change the front of the suit property.
The photographs filed by the plaintiff or the photographs filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash is not sufficient to show that the defendant had grabbed the suit property.

Further, the suit property is not identifiable from the document Ex. PW1/1 and Ex. PW1/2.
12.19.
The documents executed by Sh. Doji in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit property is GPA Ex. PW-1/1 and Will Ex. PW-1/2.

In the GPA and Will, the measurement of property is mentioned as 50 Sq. Yards, however dimension (length and width) of the property is not mentioned anywhere nor it is mentioned in GPA and Will executed by Sh. Doji as to what is situated on the north side, south side, east side and west side of the suit property measuring 50 sq. yards.
There is no identification of the property mentioned in the documents executed by Sh. Doji in favour of the plaintiff.

The plaintiff has filed site plan on record for identification of the suit property which is Ex.
PW1/3.
The site plan filed by the plaintiff Ex. PW1/3 regarding the suit property is not consistent to the site plan filed by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash in respect of the suit property.

In the site plan Ex. PW-1/3 relied by the plaintiff, on North side, the property of the defendant is shown and on South side,
'others property' is shown and on East side, there is road and on West side, there is nala.
In the plaint and affidavit, the plaintiff has not stated as to whose property is situated on South Side and it is only stated as, "others property".
The plaintiff has not stated in pleadings or his evidence as to whether the "others property" in South Side is vacant plot or constructed property.
This position regarding the "others property" on South Side in clarified by PW-2 Sh. Doji in his evidence.
PW-2 Sh. Doji has stated during his cross-examination, "Premises adjoining to my plot belong to the defendant.
There is a nala behind the plot.
Adjoining plot on the other side is vacant."
From the testimony of PW2, it appears that adjoining property on the other side (South Side) is a vacant plot of land.
However, in the site plan prepared by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash, it is mentioned that on South side of the disputed property (portion shown in green), there is room with boundary wall constructed.
No vacant plot is shown adjoining the disputed property on the South side in the site plan of PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash.
The site plan of Ex. PW4/1 would show that there is vacant plot which is second property on South side to the disputed property.
The boundaries of the suit property described by PW2 Sh. Doji is different from the boundaries shown by PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash in the site plan prepared on visit.
It is the duty of the plaintiff to describe and prove the suit property with complete description and identifiable boundaries.

However as already discussed above, the boundaries of the suit Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/
9 property is not mentioned in documents nor identification of the suit property is established from the site plan filed by the plaintiff.

sentences.text: 12.22. Suggestion given to PW-1 by Ld. Counsel for the defendant during his cross-examination, "It is further wrong to suggest that in any case, if the defendant was in possession of any property apart from his property bearing no. GA-114, the same is not the plaintiff's property" is not sufficient to prove the case of the plaintiff that the defendant had encroached upon the plot measuring 50 Sq Yards belonging to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has also examined Sh. Doji as PW-2.
PW-2 had sold the suit property to the plaintiff.
However, PW2 has not brought any document to show that he was the owner of the suit property.
In his cross-examination, PW-2 has stated that he was in possession of the plot when he sold it to the plaintiff.
He has further stated that he used to reside there (in suit property) with his family.
The testimony of PW-2 would suggest that he had got done construction in the suit property and he was residing there with his family.
His statement is inconsistent to the pleadings of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has averred in the plaint that after purchasing the suit property, he had constructed boundary walls and also constructed one small room with two doors.
However as discussed above, PW2 Sh. Doji has stated that he was living in the suit property prior to the sale of the suit property to the plaintiff.
In the cross-examination, PW2 Sh. Doji has also stated that there was some cases between him and defendant.
He has stated that the wife of the defendant has registered FIR u/s 376 IPC against him for which he was sent behind bars.
It is clear from the testimony of PW2 that there is previous enmity between the plaintiff and the defendant.
PW2 Doji is an interested witness and he has motive to depose against the defendant.
Further, the testimony of PW-2 Sh. Doji is not sufficient to show that the defendant had encroached and grabbed the suit property measuring 50 Sq Yards.
The FIR no. 755/2017 PS Sangam Vihar Ex. PW1/5 was registered on the complaint of the plaintiff.
It has come in the cross examination of PW1/plaintiff that he was not aware that in the case registered by him, the defendant has been acquitted.
The registration of FIR regarding trespass does not prove that the defendant has encroached upon the property of the plaintiff.

During course of the arguments, Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff has also relied upon the cross-examination of the defendant /DW-1 to prove that the defendant had grabbed the suit property of the plaintiff and that he has taken false defence that the plaintiff had sold the suit property to anyone.
I have gone through the cross-examination of the DW-1.

In his evidence by way of affidavit,
DW-1 has stated that the plaintiff had already sold the suit property to Sh. Jitender Nath Sinha and Sh. Jitender Nath Sinha is in possession of the suit property.

Thereafter, in his cross examination,
DW1 has stated, "Plot No. GA-113 used to belong to one Mrs. Sunita W/o Sh. Jitender Nath Sinha in the year 2011.
I do not know when Mrs. Sunita purchased the property.
Mrs. Sunita sold the said property to Sh. Radhey Shyam.
As of now, there are built up flats in property number GA-113.
I do not know about the ownership status of property no. GA-113 as of now.
" DW1 has further stated, "It Babu Lal Mewati vs Gulab Singh on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4939595/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10 is correct that property bearing no. GA 113 admeasures 50 square yards.
Vol. Documents of said property are in the name of Sunita."
The aforesaid statements made by the DW1 during his cross examination are beyond his pleadings.
The defendant has not brought any material to show that the property of the plaintiff was in possession of Sh. Jitender Nath Sinha or any other person.

However, even if the defendant is not able to prove his defence that the plaintiff had sold the suit property or that property of the plaintiff was in possession of some other person, it does not relieve the plaintiff of his burden to prove that it is the defendant who had grabbed the suit property measuring 50 Sq Yards.
Mere failure of the defendant to prove his defence does not shift the burden upon the defendant from that of the plaintiff.

Only when the plaintiff is able to discharge his onus that the property in the possession of the defendant belongs to him (plaintiff), the burden shifts upon the defendant to show that the property in his possession is not the property of the plaintiff.
In written arguments, it is submitted on behalf of the plaintiff that the defendant had sold 30 Sq Yards of his property to some third person out of 110 Sq Yards.

In para no. 3 of the plaint, the plaintiff has stated that the defendant had sold 30 sq. yards out of 110 sq. yards owned by him,
however, no such averment was made by the plaintiff in his evidence by way of affidavit.
This argument on behalf of the plaintiff is without any substance.
No material has been produced by the plaintiff to show that the defendant had sold any portion of his property to any one.
Further, during cross examination of DW1, no such question was put to him that he had sold 30 sq. yards of land to third person out of his entire property measuring 110 sq. yards.
Even the report of PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash states that the defendant had title documents of property measuring 110 Sq Yards.
As already discussed above, the testimony of the PW4 Sh. Jai Prakash and PW-2 Doji do not prove that the defendant has grabbed the property of the plaintiff ad-measuring 50 sq. yards.
Mere self serving statement of PW-1 /plaintiff without any material is not sufficient to prove that the defendant had grabbed the suit property.
Further, the plaintiff has failed to show that Sh. Doji had any title over the suit property which he could have transferred to him.
In view of the above, this Court is of the view that the plaintiff has failed to prove, on preponderance of probability, that the defendant had grabbed the property of the plaintiff.
This issue is accordingly decided in favour of the defendant and against the plaintiff.
13. Issue No. 2: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree of possession of property bearing plot no. GA 113, Pul Prahaladpur, Badarpur, New Delhi the defendant?
OPP Issue No. 3: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree of mandatory and permanent injunction as prayed for?
OPP 14.
In view of my findings on Issue no. 1, this Court holds that the plaintiff is not entitled to decree of possession or decree of mandatory or permanent injunction.
Accordingly, both issues are decided in favour of the defendant and against the plaintiff.
15. Relief:
In view of my findings on aforesaid issues, this Court holds that the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief.
